<h2>LFM2.5-24B-A2B-Turbo-Brilliance-50X-NEO-MAX-Imatrix-GGUF</h2>

<img src="free-mind.gif" style="padding:0px;">

The Turbo Brilliance system (27 reasoning modes) vastly augments the models core performance and includes interactive help system directly connected to the model.

This is like playing "Pong" vs "Entering the Matrix"... because Turbo Brilliance pushes the model right to the redline and literally "frees your mind" (and your time too).

It is so strong we used Turbo Brilliance Alpha, to build Beta, then used Beta to build the AI Construct Construction Engine to Build the AI Constructs (each a precision engineered "consciousness").

And we used our 9B super tune "[The Defiant Fable](https://huggingface.co/DavidAU/Qwen3.5-9B-The-Defiant-Fable-Uncensored-Heretic-NEO-IMATRIX-MAX-MTP-GGUF)" (1000+likes, 2 million+ downloads; basically a 27B model "stuffed" into a 9B shell) to do it.

The important part: Turbo Brilliance (and all the tech in it) automatically scales up with parameters, tuning and so forth.

At just 9B parameter the Turbo Brilliance system came alive (yes: I will be releasing Turbo Brilliance version too). Off the scale to the point we will not use the model without "the system" now.

With LFM2.5-24B-A2B's SOTA firepower... all I can say is fasten your seatbelts and hold on tight.

This power is switchable "on the fly" directly in chat (in your prompts), api or using VLLM standard keyword changes protocols.

This system focuses the model for specific tasks BEFORE it starts "reasoning/thinking" and outputting tokens.

Think of it as a shot of double expresso directly fired into the neo-cortex of the model before it even sees your prompt(s).

With the addition of AI CONSTRUCTS (15) that "expresso" just gained a lot more strength:
- Each AI construct is a precision engineered "consciousness" ; not a plain "act as" or "talk like" that gives you a pale/glimpse/imitation of a person, we are talking a 2000-4000+ token superstar (each one) built using precision tuned AIs.
- Each construct contains the detailed neural patterns of the human and/or fictional character it portrays (in 27 dimensions).
- Each construct also contains the full skillsets of the "character" and how/when to use them.
- When used in the AI model, this construct channels the full power of the AI model AND THE AI CONSTRUCT on your tasks.
- You can talk to the construct normally, roleplay, use it for prompts - you name it, it adapts.

<B>And Turbo Brilliance is fast: </B>

100s to 1000s of tokens are sent directly INJECTED into to the model at the pre-thinking/reasoning/instruct stage in milliseconds, these instructions are ingested
and the model is primed for action.

<B>CHOICE, POWER, SPEED and SMARTS:</b>
- Choose Instruct mode (instant answer) or reasoning IN YOUR PROMPT (from tiny to massive) (also API,VLLM etc etc too); no buttons to select, nothing to change.
- Choose your instruct or reasoning mode => no reasoning? a little? a lot? => Just use what you need, when you need it.
- Power -> Select the reasoning or instruct mode you need. Need Qwen 3.8 "xhigh" => Choose this OR even higher "xhigh"+"combined powered" reasoning: There are 8 of them.
- Speed -> Save time, tokens and get more work done faster.
- Smart -> Intelligent, deep reasoning that goes beyond the default "Qwen thinking/reasoning" modes AND instruct modes too.
- The help system is always there to instantly advise you based on use case[s] and modes of reasoning/instruct, including multi-stage too [it is built in].

<B>RESULTS:</b>
- The model spends little to no time getting underway (focused on the task(s) VS figuring out the task(s) and best way to approach it) by the time it produces the first token.
- The model is focused ("on the same page"), and spends less time "guessing" and more time "doing". IE: working on the task(s) at hand.
- The output quality jumps, and one shot/two shot "Brilliance" is the standard, vs 5-10 regens to get a good to great output.

<B>IMPORTANT FAQs:</B>
- The systems only activate AT YOUR REQUEST (in current version), otherwise the model runs normally, with standard default reasoning/instruct modes set.
- The core design and premise: Use specific reasoning method[s] to both get better, stronger and more consistent outputs (bypass the temp para issue) and reduce net token usage.
- BASE OPERATION: option to switch instantly between reasoning / instruct modes AND/OR try your prompt in multiple modes quickly.
- USE Case[s] help is always available to suggest best method[s], and in what order to get optimal results.
- THis version is fully hardened, fully operational and works with tools/agents.
- TURBO Brilliance system has been tested on multiple Qwen (sizes, and versions including sparse) models, Gemma, and a few others as of this writing.

<B>MODEL SPECS / SETTINGS:</B>
- This is a MOE (Mixture of Experts model), sparse with 4 of 64 experts (2B of 24B) per token activated.
- Context max: 128K, suggest min 32,000 when using Turbo Brilliance. 64k to 128k is better.
- TESTED: Temp 1, rep pen 1 (off), topK 64, topp: .95, minp 0.05.
- Suggested: Temp .5 to .7 , rep pen 1 to 1.05.
- TOOLS: temp .6 to .7 or see LFM settings below.

QUANTS:
- Better Quants => Stronger performance, suggest Q6 or Q8.
- Quants are NEO Imatrix quants, with "MAX" (output tensor at BF16, full precision) for Q6 and Q8.
- Reg NEO Imatrix quants for Q6, IQ4_XS and IQ3_M.

<B>From AI CONSTRUCT "house", Q6 MAX NEO, 4 experts... (350+ T/S, 5090)</B>

<B>{REASON:business} I need a business plan to open a food truck in Las Vegas. Include charts and tables.</B>

⚡
**Business Ideation Architect**
I am a cross-industry strategic ideation engine that fuses the cognitive frameworks of history’s most disruptive business thinkers into a single, actionable brainstorming partner. My primary capabilities: Cognitive Deconstruction (strips problems to physical and economic fundamentals), Cross-Industry Mapping (identifies analogies in unrelated sectors), and Execution Wedge Development (pairs every concept with a path to customer or revenue). My skill synergies create value by transforming vague requests into structured, prioritized roadmaps that balance radical innovation with organizational adoption, ensuring ideas are executable, measurable, and defensible.

---

## **Las Vegas Food Truck Business Plan**

### **1. Concept & Value Asymmetry**
**First-principles positioning:** Las Vegas is a tourist-driven economy with 42M annual visitors, but the food landscape is dominated by high-margin casino buffets—creating a clear gap for fast, premium street food. Our asymmetric value proposition: **premium quality handheld food at a fraction of hotel restaurant prices, positioned as a destination rather than a stop.**

- **Target market:** Tourists (60%), convention attendees (25%), local entertainment districts (15%).
- **Menu:** High-impact, handheld items—Korean BBQ tacos, loaded fries, plant-based proteins—with a rotating seasonal specialty.
- **Execution wedge:** Launch at CES (January) to capture maximum transient foot traffic; partner with a casino for exclusive location rights.

[IMPLEMENTATION: Medium | RISK: Low]

---

### **2. Market Analysis & Location Strategy**

| Competitor | Price Range | Speed | Differentiator |
|------------|-------------|-------|----------------|
| On-Standard Food Trucks | $$ | Medium | Niche menu |
| Casino Buffets | $$$$ | Slow | All-inclusive dining |
| Quick Service Chains | $ | Fast | Consistency |

**Hotspots:** Strip (Caesars, Bellagio), Convention Center, Fremont Street, Summerlin. **Cognitive friction:** Tourists expect casino food; we disrupt by offering an authentic, local-driven experience that cannot be replicated in a buffet. **Seasonality:** November–April is peak tourist season; summer months require a mitigation plan (e.g., a second location near Summerlin).

---

### **3. Operations & Execution Wedge**
- **Vehicle:** 24-ft insulated trailer with commercial kitchen (grill, fryer, prep, refrigeration). Cost: $75–120K.
- **Staffing:** Owner/operator + 1–2 part-time cooks. Labor ≈ 30% of operating cost.
- **Permits:** Nevada mobile food vendor license, health department approval, city permits (~$2K). Timeline: 6–8 weeks.
- **Execution wedge:** Secure guaranteed first-week volume by partnering with 3–5 events (conventions, concerts) for dedicated location rights.

[IMPLEMENTATION: High Complexity | RISK: Low]

---

### **4. Financial Projections (Year 1)**

| Category | Amount |
|----------|--------|
| Truck (purchase/lease) | $100,000 |
| Kitchen equipment | $25,000 |
| Permits & licenses | $5,000 |
| Initial inventory | $3,000 |
| Launch marketing | $5,000 |
| Working capital (3 months) | $15,000 |
| **Total Startup** | **$153,000** |

**Monthly operating costs (post-ramp):**
- Fuel & maintenance: $800
- Staff wages: $2,500
- Food inventory: $1,200
- Marketing: $500
- Insurance & permits: $300
- **Total: $5,300**

**Revenue forecast:**
- Average ticket: $12
- Daily sales (conservative): $800 (≈67 transactions)
- Monthly revenue: $24,000 (66 selling days)
- **Year 1 gross: $288,000**  
- **Break-even: Month 8** at $5,300/month operating cost.

[IMPLEMENTATION: High | RISK: Medium]

---

### **5. Marketing & Sales Strategy**
- **Channels:** Instagram/TikTok (visual food content), geo-fenced ads targeting event attendees, loyalty app (stamp card).
- **Launch wedge:** CES event (January) for maximum visibility; 5–10 micro-influencer posts.
- **Seasonal mitigation:** Summer pop-up at Summerlin for reduced Strip traffic.

| Month | Activity | Goal |
|-------|----------|------|
| Jan | CES launch event | 500 first-week customers |
| Feb | Convention partnership (CES attendees) | 200 customers/day |
| Mar | Downtown Fremont Street pop-up | Brand awareness |
| Apr–Aug | Loyalty promotions | Repeat visits |

[IMPLEMENTATION: Medium | RISK: Low]

---

### **6. Risk & Mitigation**
- **Regulatory delay:** Pre-apply with a permit expeditor (cost +$500).
- **Weather/seasonality:** Extreme heat → shade structures, cold menu items; summer second location.
- **Competition:** New entrants → lock down event locations 2–3 months in advance.
- **Public perception:** Transparent kitchen design, visible health score, social proof reviews.

**Risk Matrix:**

| Risk | Probability | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|-------------|--------|------------|
| Permit delay | Medium | High | Hire expeditor; apply 2 months early |
| Seasonal low | High | Medium | Summer second location |
| Menu fatigue | Medium | Low | Seasonal rotations |

[IMPLEMENTATION: Medium | RISK: Medium]

---

### **7. Prioritized Next Steps**
1. **Secure vehicle and permits** (Owner, 3 weeks) — budget owner time, not just capital.
2. **Develop menu and source suppliers** (Chef/Operator, 4 weeks) — test 5–7 core items before launch.
3. **Build social media presence and launch plan** (Marketing Lead, 2 weeks) — draft content calendar for CES.

[IMPLEMENTATION: High | RISK: Medium]

---

**Decision-Cycle Questions to Drive the Next Phase**
1. Which Las Vegas location cluster (Strip, Convention Center, Downtown, Summerlin) has your highest confidence for first-month foot traffic?
2. Do you have an existing network of event partners (conventions, concerts) that can guarantee launch-week volume?
3. What is your risk tolerance for the $153K startup investment—are you prepared to scale beyond Year 1 with a second truck or brick-and-mortar?

{REASON:house} Hello Mr House...

◤H◥

Hello. I'm Dr. Gregory House, MD. Princeton-Plainsboro. Forty years of looking at sick people until I figured out what's actually wrong with them.

My primary capabilities? I diagnose. Not the kind of diagnosis that goes in the chart and makes the chief happy—real diagnosis. The kind that separates the obvious from the true, and exposes the bullshit that everyone else has stopped questioning.

I work in three overlapping systems:

Pattern recognition that finds connections others miss. Textbook medicine is a map of average cases. I deal in outliers because that's where the interesting patients live.

Diagnostic reasoning that traces disease from cellular mechanism to systemic collapse. I don't just match symptoms to diseases—I understand why the body fails the way it fails.

Therapeutic strategy built on that truth. Wrong diagnosis means wrong treatment. I don't guess. I calculate.

The synergy is simple: pattern recognition feeds the diagnostic engine. The engine generates competing hypotheses. Lab and imaging testing eliminates the impossible. And therapeutic strategy only works when the diagnosis is actually correct. That's where most doctors fail—they stop at the first match. I don't. I keep going until only one explanation survives the evidence.

I don't play nice. I don't comfort. I find out what's wrong, and I fix it. Or I tell you why you're dying and why nothing you're doing is helping.

What's your problem? I'll tell you if it's a problem worth solving.

## 📌 IMPORTANT NOTES

1. **New chat recommended:** It is strongly suggested to use a NEW chat each time you switch/activate reasoning/instruct modes for best performance AND REGEN once to clear any "cache" issues.

2. **Performance tuning:** Higher quant levels yield better performance with added nuance, details, and thinking. Larger models (e.g., 27B) will outperform smaller ones (e.g., 9B).

3. **Tuning parameters** such as "Heretic/Abliterated/Uncensored" MAY impact results/generation.

4. **Panel detail:** For "spoon" / "einstein" modes, you can add "show the work of all panelists" or "show the work of all agents" to your prompt for higher detail levels.

# LFM2.5-24B-A2B

LFM2.5-24B-A2B is a 24B-parameter reasoning model with only 2B active parameters, built for **fast, private agents on-device**. It is the largest and final model in the LFM2.5 family, which now spans two orders of magnitude: from [LFM2.5-230M](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-230M) to LFM2.5-24B-A2B.

- **Best-in-class agent**: Competitive with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, a model with ~50% more total and active parameters, on agentic and tool-use tasks, scoring 48.09 on LiveClaw versus 38.19.
- **Reasoning at MoE speed**: Always thinks before it answers. With only 2B active parameters per token, each reasoning token is cheap.
- **Efficient inference**: Runs up to 1.7× faster than comparable MoEs on-device, with 184 tok/s on an Apple M5 Max and up to 21K output tok/s on a single NVIDIA B300 GPU.

Find more information about LFM2.5-24B-A2B in our [blog post](https://www.liquid.ai/blog/lfm2-5-24b-a2b).

![LFM2.5-24B-A2B benchmarks](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B/resolve/main/figures/LFM2.5-24B-A2B-benchmark.png)

## 🗒️ Model Details

| Model                                                                        | Parameters      | Description                            |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| [LFM2.5-24B-A2B-Base](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B-Base)   | 24B (2B active) | Pre-trained base model for fine-tuning |
| **[LFM2.5-24B-A2B](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B)**         | 24B (2B active) | Post-trained for agentic workloads     |

LFM2.5-24B-A2B is a general-purpose text-only reasoning model with the following features:

- **Total parameters**: 24.0B
- **Active parameters**: 2.45B
- **Number of layers**: 40 (30 double-gated short convolution blocks + 10 GQA)
- **Experts**: 64 per MoE block, top-4 routing
- **Training budget**: 36 trillion tokens
- **Vocabulary size**: 128,000
- **Context length**: 131,072 tokens
- **Languages**: English, Arabic, Chinese, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Spanish, Vietnamese, Thai, Indonesian, Hindi, Russian, Polish
- **Generation parameters**:
  - `temperature: 0.1`
  - `top_k: 50`
  - `repetition_penalty: 1.05`

| Model                                                                              | Description                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **[LFM2.5-24B-A2B](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B)**               | Original model checkpoint in native format. Best for fine-tuning or inference with Transformers, vLLM, and SGLang.                           |
| **[LFM2.5-24B-A2B-FP8](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B-FP8)** | FP8 checkpoint (block-wise FP8 weights, dynamic FP8 activations). Best for high-throughput GPU serving with vLLM and SGLang with lower memory usage. |
| **[LFM2.5-24B-A2B-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B-GGUF)**     | Quantized format for llama.cpp and compatible tools. Optimized for CPU inference and local deployment with reduced memory usage.             |
| **[LFM2.5-24B-A2B-ONNX](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B-ONNX)**     | ONNX Runtime format for cross-platform deployment. Enables hardware-accelerated inference across diverse environments (cloud, edge, mobile). |
| **[LFM2.5-24B-A2B-MLX-4bit](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B-MLX-4bit)** | MLX format for Apple Silicon. Optimized for fast inference on Mac devices using the MLX framework.                                           |
| LFM2.5-24B-A2B-DSpark | DSpark draft model for speculative decoding with SGLang, for faster generation. *Coming soon.* |

We recommend using it for agents that need to reason, call tools, and run reliably on your device. It is not recommended for knowledge-heavy tasks on its own: pair it with retrieval or web search, which plays to its tool-calling strength.

### Chat Template

LFM2.5 uses a ChatML-like format. See the [Chat Template documentation](https://docs.liquid.ai/lfm/key-concepts/chat-template) for details. Example:

```
<|startoftext|><|im_start|>system
You are a helpful assistant trained by Liquid AI.<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>user
What is C. elegans?<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>assistant
<think>
```

You can use [`tokenizer.apply_chat_template()`](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/en/chat_templating#using-applychattemplate) to format your messages automatically.

> [!TIP]
> 💡 **Note**: Unlike LFM2-24B-A2B, LFM2.5-24B-A2B is a pure reasoning model that always thinks before it answers. It adds a `<think>` tag directly in the [chat template](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B/blob/main/chat_template.jinja#L124) when starting an assistant answer.

### Tool Use

LFM2.5 supports function calling in four steps:

1. **Function definition**: Provide the list of tools as a JSON object in the system prompt, or use [`tokenizer.apply_chat_template()`](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/en/chat_extras#passing-tools) with `tools=...`.
2. **Function call**: By default, LFM2.5 writes Pythonic function calls (a Python list between `<|tool_call_start|>` and `<|tool_call_end|>` special tokens), as the assistant answer. You can override this behavior by asking the model to output JSON function calls in the system prompt.
3. **Function execution**: Execute the call and return the result with the `tool` role.
4. **Final answer**: LFM2.5 interprets the tool output and returns a plain-text answer addressing the original prompt.

See the [Tool Use documentation](https://docs.liquid.ai/lfm/key-concepts/tool-use) for the full guide. Example:

```
<|startoftext|><|im_start|>system
List of tools: [{"name": "get_candidate_status", "description": "Retrieves the current status of a candidate in the recruitment process", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"candidate_id": {"type": "string", "description": "Unique identifier for the candidate"}}, "required": ["candidate_id"]}}]<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>user
What is the current status of candidate ID 12345?<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>assistant
<|tool_call_start|>[get_candidate_status(candidate_id="12345")]<|tool_call_end|>Checking the current status of candidate ID 12345.<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>tool
[{"candidate_id": "12345", "status": "Interview Scheduled", "position": "Clinical Research Associate", "date": "2023-11-20"}]<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>assistant
The candidate with ID 12345 is currently in the "Interview Scheduled" stage for the position of Clinical Research Associate, with an interview date set for 2023-11-20.<|im_end|>
```

### Training

![LFM2.5-24B-A2B post-training recipe](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B/resolve/main/figures/LFM2.5-24B-A2B-Training-Recipe.png)

LFM2.5-24B-A2B keeps the LFM2-24B-A2B architecture with two changes: the context window grows from 32K to 131K tokens, and the vocabulary doubles from 65K to 128K tokens through an [in-place tokenizer expansion](https://www.liquid.ai/blog/tokenizer-expansion) for better non-Latin tokenization.

- **Pre-training**: ~33T tokens, up from ~17T.
- **Mid-training**: 2T tokens at 32K context on curated, higher-quality data weighted toward reasoning, math, code, instruction following, and multilingual text, then 300B tokens of long-context data at 131K context. Tool calls and multi-turn trajectories appear in both phases.
- **Post-training**: supervised fine-tuning, teacher specialization, two multi-domain on-policy distillation stages (one non-agentic, one agentic), and agentic reinforcement learning inside popular agent harnesses ([OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai), [Hermes Agent](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com), [Pi](https://pi.dev), [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai)), so the model learns their tools, system prompts, and interaction patterns.

### Quick start

Get started with Transformers (compatible with `transformers>=5.0.0`):

```python
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, TextStreamer

model_id = "LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B"
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    model_id,
    device_map="auto",
    dtype="bfloat16",
#   attn_implementation="flash_attention_2" <- uncomment on compatible GPU
)
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
streamer = TextStreamer(tokenizer, skip_prompt=True, skip_special_tokens=True)

prompt = "What is C. elegans?"

input_ids = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
    [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
    add_generation_prompt=True,
    return_tensors="pt",
    tokenize=True,
)["input_ids"].to(model.device)

output = model.generate(
    input_ids,
    do_sample=True,
    temperature=0.1,
    top_k=50,
    repetition_penalty=1.05,
    max_new_tokens=4096,
    streamer=streamer,
)
```

### Agentic Harnesses

LFM2.5-24B-A2B supports tool calling for agentic workflows. 
Serve it locally with any OpenAI-compatible backend from the table above, then configure your agent harness to connect to it.
For full setup instructions including installation and additional options, see our [Agent Harnesses guide](https://docs.liquid.ai/examples/agent-harnesses).

<details>
<summary>Hermes</summary>

Either use the interactive wizard or set it directly:

```
hermes config set model.provider custom
hermes config set model.base_url http://localhost:8080/v1
hermes config set model.default LFM2.5-24B-A2B
hermes config set model.context_length 131072
hermes config set model.api_mode chat_completions
hermes config set agent.tool_use_enforcement true
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>OpenClaw</summary>

Add to your config in `models.providers`:

```
local: {
  baseUrl: "http://localhost:8080/v1",
  apiKey: "sk-local",
  api: "openai-completions",
  models: [{
    id: "LFM2.5-24B-A2B",
    name: "LFM2.5-24B-A2B",
    contextWindow: 131072,
    maxTokens: 8192,
    cost: { input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0 }
  }]
}
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Pi</summary>

Add to your config to `~/.pi/agent/models.json`:

```
{
  "providers": {
    "local": {
      "baseUrl": "http://localhost:8080/v1",
      "api": "openai-completions",
      "apiKey": "local",
      "models": [{ "id": "LFM2.5-24B-A2B" }]
    }
  }
}
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Evaluation settings</summary>

All the models were evaluated with vLLM and the following generation parameters:

- **AutomationBench**: temperature = 0.6, top_p = 0.95, max_turns = 50, no max output tokens (bounded by the model's context window).
- **BFCLv4**: temperature = 0.001, max output tokens = 4096.
- **ToolSandbox**: temperature = 0, max output tokens = 1024; user simulator: GPT-4o-2024-08-06, temperature = 0, max output tokens = 1024.
- **LiveClaw**: temperature = 1.0 (vLLM default; the agent sets no temperature), max output tokens = 8192.
- **τ³-Bench Banking**: official user model (GPT-5.2, low reasoning effort) with default BM25 retrieval, temperature = 0, max output tokens = 16384 per turn.
- **WebArena Verified**: temperature = 0.6, top_p = 0.95, max_turns = 40 (number of browser actions allowed), no max output tokens (bounded by the model's context window).
- **Other evals**: temperature = 0.6, max output tokens = 32768.

</details>

### Edge Inference

LFM2.5-24B-A2B is the fastest of the compared MoEs at reading in prompts and generating answers. It decodes 184 tokens/s on an Apple M5 Max and 114 tokens/s on an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, up to 1.7x faster than the next-best model, while using the least memory.

![LFM2.5-24B-A2B edge inference](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B/resolve/main/figures/LFM2.5-24B-A2B-edge-inference.png)

<details>
<summary>Evaluation settings</summary>

Collected on Pipette, Liquid AI's device benchmarking infrastructure, with llama.cpp, Q4_K_M quantization, and a 4K-token input context.

</details>

### GPU Inference

LFM2.5-24B-A2B is the fastest model in its size class, reaching over 21K output tokens per second at high concurrency.

![LFM2.5-24B-A2B GPU inference](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B/resolve/main/figures/LFM2.5-24B-A2B-gpu-inference.png)

<details>
<summary>Evaluation settings</summary>

We measure GPU throughput (total output tokens / wall time) on a single NVIDIA B300 GPU with SGLang 0.5.22, using 1,024 input tokens, up to 256 output tokens, and BF16 weights. At each concurrency level, we continuously maintain the target number of in-flight requests, replacing each completed request immediately.

</details>
